To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) adversarial training is highly sensitive to the training settings and 2) the proposed improvements are not always better than simply early stopping.

(i) the basic training settings (e.g. weight decay, training schedules, etc.) used by AT methods are inconsistent and highly affect the robust accuracy, and (ii) a simple baseline setting can achieve new state-of-art results on CIFAR- 10

(1) weight decay is a crucial factor for AT; (2) the training schedule is also important, especially when using a small learning rate (e.g., 1e-3); and (3) the training schedule and the weight decay should be carefully tuned for each model.

the basic training tricks of AT, which is of great significance to both the research community and industry.
the implementation details of adversarially trained defenses, and we believe it will help the community to better understand and evaluate adversarial robustness in future research.
the following questions: What are the most critical factors that determine the adversarial robustness of a model? How to properly benchmark the defenses in a fair way?

adversarial robust models are more sensitive to the implementation details than previously thought.
the most important tricks for adversarially training robust models are weight decay and learning rate scheduling.
the robustness of a model is highly sensitive to the training settings and hyperparameters, which should be considered carefully.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adversarial robust training is much more complicated than we thought.
the training tricks for adversarial training are more important than we thought.
the bag of tricks for training robust models is not as simple as we think.

, in order to fairly evaluate and compare adversarially trained networks, one should be very careful to the overlooked training details.
the robustness of a model is not solely determined by the proposed method itself but is more influenced by the training setting, especially when we compare the results from different methods.
we need more careful evaluations and a unified baseline for AT methods.
